findings.quote: Her digs showed the ground further down was entirely without roots.
findings.note: BLIND: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE, pick=B. The absolutizer 'entirely' marks C as strippable on sight; a solver with no domain knowledge and no passage drops it immediately.

findings.quote: She traced most of the lift to fine roots under the stones.
findings.note: BLIND cont. Standard arboricultural knowledge decides the rest: pavement heave comes from fine roots proliferating in the moist layer directly under the slabs, not from severed structural roots (D). A (an inconclusive result) is further undercut by q5 option C, whose main-idea statement asserts the text does explain why paving rises. Distractors stay substantive, so flag rather than kill.

findings.quote: They had nothing obvious in common beyond their age.
findings.note: BLIND: PARTIALLY, pick=C. Three options name a concrete physical cause and C alone denies a pattern, and it is also the only hedged option ('nothing obvious'). Odd-one-out plus sole-hedge gives a test-wise solver a materially better-than-chance pick with no passage, though B (a badly relaid water main) remains substantively live.

findings.quote: They will never have to be taken up again.
findings.note: BLIND: STRUCTURAL_LEAK, pick=A. 'never' is a bare absolutizer; the option self-destructs on form.

findings.quote: Their paving has not shifted at all since the work was done.
findings.note: BLIND cont. 'not ... at all' is a second absolutizer in the same option set, so two of the four options strip on sight without any passage.

findings.quote: The trial has no direct view of what is happening beneath them.
findings.note: BLIND cont. The surviving pair is then decided by form alone: the stem asks what is IMPLIED, and D asserts a concrete positive fact that a text would state rather than imply, while A is a near-tautological epistemic limit (you cannot see under intact paving) and the sole hedged option. Answerable with zero domain knowledge and no passage.

findings.quote: She thinks the results bore it out in full.
findings.note: BLIND: PARTIALLY, pick=B. 'in full' strips C. B is then the sole two-sided option among flat stances, the stem presupposes the writer has an attitude (weakening D's neutrality), and the sibling stems establish mixed results ('where the treatment failed' in q2 versus 'where the treatment has worked' in q3), which points at a split verdict. A stays live, so flag not kill.

findings.quote: What are we told about the five streets where the treatment failed?
findings.note: BLIND: STRUCTURAL_LEAK, pick=C. This sibling stem asserts on the face of the question sheet that the treatment failed on five streets, which contradicts q5 option B ('How one city's engineers finally beat the tree roots under its pavements'). No passage is needed to eliminate B.

findings.quote: The rising cost to councils of people tripping over uneven paving.
findings.note: BLIND cont. Neither A nor D is touched by any of the unit's four other stems, which are all about the root findings, the failed streets, the working streets and the Fearnbeck dispute; a solver eliminates both from the question sheet alone.

findings.quote: Why paving rises over tree roots, and how one city’s remedy has fared.
findings.note: BLIND cont. C is the neutral umbrella that semantically contains the remaining scope: 'how one city's remedy has fared' covers both the failures and the successes the sibling stems reveal. Umbrella option plus three form-eliminated distractors makes this main-idea item answerable by pure form.

findings.quote: price
findings.note: BLIND: PARTIALLY, pick=C. 'price', 'charge' and 'cost' are near-interchangeable in most monetary frames, so a well-formed cloze cannot key any one of them uniquely; 'toll' stands apart as the only member with a distinct figurative sense ('take a toll'). The solver narrows to the odd one out with no context whatsoever.

findings.quote: It made the loft weathertight the year round, whatever the weather drove against the roof.
findings.note: BLIND: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE, pick=D. 'the year round, whatever the weather' is an absolutizer overclaim that strips on sight, and A and D are exact opposites (torching shelters the battens versus torching holds wet against them) - the classic polar pair in which the key sits.

findings.quote: It held the wet it took up against the battens, and the wood rotted there.
findings.note: BLIND cont. Building-conservation knowledge decides it: torching, the lime mortar pointed under the tiles, is a well-known cause of batten decay precisely because the mortar holds moisture against the timber. A is a substantive opposing position rather than filler, so this is world-knowledge answerability, not a structural kill.

findings.quote: After 1851 a whole box in the middle aisle could be had for two shillings a year.
findings.note: BLIND: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE, pick=B. D is a bare datum, not a conclusion, so it fails the stem's 'What can be concluded' frame and drops on form; worse, the datum it supplies (a whole prime middle-aisle box for two shillings a year, after 1851) reads as collapsed demand and corroborates option B from inside the option set.

findings.quote: Letting seats singly was the wardens' way of filling pews that would no longer let whole.
findings.note: BLIND cont. Nineteenth-century pew-rent history - falling rents, the post-1851 free-seat movement, wardens subdividing pews they could no longer let whole - points to B. A is its polar opposite (excess demand) and C a substantive social alternative, so flag rather than kill.

findings.quote: Stenen fräste sönder till ett vitt pulver.
findings.note: BLIND: RECALL_ONLY, pick=A. Textbook chemistry: slaking quicklime is exothermic and the lumps hiss and fall apart to a white powder. Anyone with school chemistry answers without any text; the passage is decoration and no comprehension is measured.

findings.quote: Vattnet drev koldioxiden ur stenen.
findings.note: BLIND cont. The distractors are not competing positions but plain chemical errors - carbon dioxide is driven off by heat during burning, not by water during slaking (C); B describes a different step of the process and D's 'hårdnade genast' is false of slaked lime - so nothing is left for a passage to ground.

findings.quote: Att kalken till största delen behölls för husbehov.
findings.note: BLIND: PARTIALLY, pick=D. C answers a different question from the stem's 'hur arbetet vid en ugn var ordnat' - it is about what became of the lime, not how the work was organised - and it also contradicts q3 option B's 'viktig binäring'. It drops on form, leaving A and D as the polar pair (a kiln per farm versus a shared kiln).

findings.quote: Att flera hushåll gick samman kring en gemensam ugn.
findings.note: BLIND cont. Swedish rural-history knowledge (kilns fired communally by a village's farms) plus q4 option C, which presupposes more surviving remains than simultaneously working kilns, points at D. A remains substantively live, so flag.

findings.quote: Utan kalkugnarna hade landsbygdens penninghushållning brutit samman.
findings.note: BLIND: STRUCTURAL_LEAK, pick=B. An extreme counterfactual overclaim ('hade ... brutit samman') that strips on sight with no passage.

findings.quote: Kalkens viktigaste användning var att förbättra jorden på åkrarna.
findings.note: BLIND cont. Superlative claim ('viktigaste') - a second strippable overclaim in the same set, leaving B as the sole moderate, two-part statement under an 'överensstämmer bäst' stem.

findings.quote: Vad kan man, utifrån texten, dra för slutsats om ugnsresterna i Klyvingetrakten?
findings.note: BLIND cont. This sibling stem presupposes surviving kiln remains in the landscape, which is verbatim the second half of option B ('vars spår ännu syns i landskapet'). Another question's stem confirms the key's content, so the item is decided from the question sheet alone.

findings.quote: Att trakten en gång sålde mer kalk än någon annan bygd i landet.
findings.note: BLIND: PARTIALLY, pick=C. The superlative absolute ('mer kalk än någon annan bygd i landet') strips A, and D's claim that the remains can be dated without excavation is implausible on its face. Under a 'dra för slutsats' stem the surviving pair favours C, the only option that reasons about the evidence rather than asserting a new fact; B stays live, so flag.

findings.quote: Den bygger på ett enda kvällsbesök i augusti.
findings.note: BLIND: PARTIALLY, pick=B. A, C and D all attack the arithmetic inputs of the calculation (fixture count, already-replaced lamps, hourly cost); B alone attacks its empirical basis, so it is the form-visible odd one out. A and D would in any case mean the saving is understated, which cuts against the author's own case.

findings.quote: Släckningen kan godtas på sommaren men bör hävas vintertid.
findings.note: BLIND cont. Lexical bridge inside the unit: 'augusti' in this question's option B pairs with the summer/winter axis of q2 option B, letting a solver mark both keys together without reading the text.

findings.quote: Belysningen bör lysa till klockan 23 året om.
findings.note: BLIND: PARTIALLY, pick=B. A is the maximalist demand ('året om') and D the bluntly dismissive counter-stance; both are poles a debate author would not hold, so a form-only solver is immediately down to the two concessive middles.

findings.quote: Släckningen kan godtas på sommaren men bör hävas vintertid.

findings.quote: Att platserna fördelades efter gårdarnas mantal också i de socknar där de bevarade protokollen bara ger knapphändiga upplysningar.

findings.quote: Han avfärdar rangläsningen och stannar för den förklaring som utgår från roddens teknik.

findings.quote: Han finner både den sociala och den praktiska läsningen möjliga och avstår från att välja mellan dem.
findings.note: BLIND cont. Material narrowing rather than a decided answer, so flag.
